Workshops & Training Events

Review past and upcoming training schools, hands-on scanner assemblies, and community education workshops led by the IMAGINE team.

June 2026 Cape Town, South Africa

IMAGINE Summer School & ISMRM Cape Town 2026

The 2026 IMAGINE Summer School was held in Cape Town, South Africa, aligned with the ISMRM 2026 Conference.

During this event, the ERNIE 1 scanner was re-assembled and calibrated, and its field homogeneity was mapped using the completed field mapping robot. The workshop successfully demonstrated that two independent sites (in Uganda/South Africa and Montreal) can build identical, high-performance educational scanners using identical open hardware parts, proving the reproducibility of the ERNIE design.

Participating Sites

University of Cape TownMbarara University of Science & Technology (MUST)The Neuro (Montreal Neurological Institute)South African Medical Research Council

February 2026 Montreal, Canada

Montreal Hands-on Workshops (ERNIE 2)

Under the leadership of researcher Maureen Nayebare, a series of hands-on educational workshops were conducted across several major biomedical research institutions in Montreal.

These sessions focused on the construction and testing of the ERNIE 2 kit. Over several weeks, students and engineers at the Montreal Neurological Institute (The Neuro), Montreal General Hospital, Polytechnique Montréal, and the Douglas Mental Health University Institute successfully assembled the 7-ring magnet array and calibrated the field mapping robot. The workshops provided local students with direct exposure to low-field MRI engineering, system integration, and hardware troubleshooting.

Participating Sites

Montreal Neurological Institute (The Neuro)Montreal General HospitalPolytechnique MontréalDouglas Mental Health University Institute

May 2025 Vienna, Austria

IMAGINE Summer School & ESMRMB Workshop 2025

The 2025 IMAGINE Summer School kicked off with a hands-on pre-congress workshop at the ESMRMB 2025 Conference in Vienna, Austria.

Trainees from Africa, Europe, and North America gathered to perform the first live, on-site assembly of the ERNIE 1 scanner. The session focused on the fundamentals of low-field MRI physics, design thinking strategies, and practical training in assembling Halbach arrays and circuit boards.

Participating Sites

Mbarara University of Science & Technology (MUST)The Neuro (Montreal Neurological Institute)Polytechnique MontréalDouglas Research Centre

IMAGINE Project

An open-source preclinical MRI initiative of the Consortium for Advancement of MRI Education and Research in Africa (CAMERA). Sustaining diagnostic health equity globally.

Open Science Compliance

All hardware files are released under open-source hardware licenses. This project is developed to satisfy the requirements of the Open Source Imaging Initiative (OSI²).
